thread:
IncidentBot: ALERT: p99 spike detected for SolisCorp in eu-west (dedicated pool: solis-euw-1). p95 ~ 3x baseline, errors steady. paging @Sanjay Patel @Maya R @Kevin Nguyen :rotating_light:
Sanjay Patel: on it. looking at dashboards now — can someone confirm if this is KV cache churn or a traffic burst?
Maya R: appears to be request surge from tenant=solis-corp, steady high concurrency on /v1/generate endpoint. rate ~ 2.8k rps to that pool since 10:02 UTC.
Kevin Nguyen: thanks. CPU on solis-euw-1 GPUs at ~92%, queue depth growing. p99 latency hits when queue > 18.
Lia Chen: throwing up the quick telemetry snippet: ```
# metrics slice
tenant=solis-corp, pool=solis-euw-1
p95: 420ms -> 1.3s
p99: 900ms -> 3.8s
gpu_util: 86% -> 92%
req_rate: 800 -> 2800 rps
```
Sanjay Patel: customer impact? Are errors user-facing or just higher tails?
Maya R: 2% 500s on some tail requests (KV eviction races). Most requests succeed but timeouts for streaming clients. Solis support reporting degraded UI.
Ops Pager: paging on-call SRE now (escalation 2). ETA for SRE to jump: ~2m.
Kevin Nguyen: mitigation options:
- short term: apply per-tenant token-bucket to drop non-critical calls (reduces burst)
- medium: migrate tenant traffic to warm spare pool `pool-eu-warm-2` (no deploy, just routing change)
- long term: increase reserved capacity for SolisCorp or autoscale buffer
Maya R: we should try migration first — less customer-visible than dropping calls. I'll prep routing update.
Lia Chen: ops steps to reroute (needs infra-admin): ```
# reroute tenant to warm pool
infractl tenant route --tenant solis-corp --from-pool solis-euw-1 --to-pool pool-eu-warm-2 --drain-connections 60
# healthcheck after switch
infractl pool health --pool pool-eu-warm-2
```
Sanjay Patel: tagging @Kevin for approval on cross-pool migration and @Lia to run infractl. Kevin?
Kevin Nguyen: approve. make it a rolling migrate with 5% ramp every 20s. watch p95/p99 and GPU util.
Maya R: starting config prep now. I'll open a short canary at 5%.
IncidentBot: NOTE: apply canary policy `canary.ramp=5%` and enable fallback `fallback.model=redwood-small` for streaming connections during migration.
Lia Chen: executing initial reroute command (canary): ```
infractl tenant route --tenant solis-corp --from-pool solis-euw-1 --to-pool pool-eu-warm-2 --ramp 5% --drain 30
```
Lia Chen: canary traffic live at 5% — monitoring.
Maya R: p95 down to 1.1s in canary, p99 slightly improved. no errors yet.
Sanjay Patel: continue ramp to 50% if stable for 2 minutes. Lia, keep an eye on queue depth.
Lia Chen: ramping to 25% now. infractl shows steady throughput.
Kevin Nguyen: CPU on source pool dropping to 78% as we shift. warm pool GPUs at 65% now. Good.
Maya R: after 3m at 25% — p95 improved globally to ~700ms, p99 trending down.
Lia Chen: ramped to 50%. monitoring for any request failures.
Ops Pager: SRE joined (SRE Oncall) — client reported degraded UI cleared for some users.
Sanjay Patel: start a short incident summary for handoff: cause apparent = tenant traffic burst; mitigation = cross-pool migration; next steps = observe for 30m, consider reserved capacity or rate-limits.
Kevin Nguyen: agree. schedule follow-up with Solutions for SolisCorp tomorrow to discuss committed capacity.
Maya R: Customer success notified. Solis support pinged with message: "We detected elevated latency for your service in eu-west; we've rerouted traffic to a warm pool to restore responsiveness and are monitoring. Will follow up with root cause & options."
IncidentBot: ACTION: assign post-incident RCA to @Maya R and @Kevin Nguyen. severity: P2.
Lia Chen: final check — now at 100% migrated. solis-euw-1 GPU util ~60%, pool-eu-warm-2 ~78%. p95 380-700ms range, p99 under 1.1s.
Sanjay Patel: handing off to on-call for night watch. summary for next shift: "SolisCorp experienced tenant-origin surge causing p99 spikes in eu-west. We migrated traffic to warm pool (completed ramp); system stable, monitor for reoccurrence; consider capacity commit."
Ops Pager: oncall handoff noted. tagging @SRE Night for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
